Groups of order seventy (C70​, D70​, D14​×C5​, D10​×C7​)

Words: 114
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
These are all the groups of group order 70 up to group isomorphism, with Dn​ denoting a dihedral group of order n. The Sylow theorems make the Sylow subgroups of orders five and seven unique: the possible counts divide fourteen and ten, respectively, and only one has the required residue. These normal subgroups of coprime order commute, giving a normal subgroup N≅C35​. Cauchy's theorem for finite groups provides an element of order two outside N, so G=N⋊C2​.
The automorphism of a finite cyclic group defining this semidirect product is a unit a modulo 35 with a2≡1. The Chinese remainder theorem makes its restrictions modulo five and seven independently +1 or −1. The resulting exponents are 1,34,6,29, giving the four displayed groups in order. Their center of a group orders are 70,1,5,7, so no two are isomorphic. Every case exists as the specified semidirect product.

Groups of order at most six (C1​,C2​,C3​,C4​,C2​×C2​,C5​,C6​,S3​)

Words: 186
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
Up to group isomorphism, the finite groups with at most six elements are the trivial group, the cyclic groups C2​,C3​,C4​,C5​,C6​, the Klein four-group C2​×C2​, and the symmetric group S3​.
A group of prime cardinality is a cyclic group, since Lagrange's theorem forces any nonidentity element to generate it. For four elements, either an element has order of a group element four, or every nonidentity element is an involution. In the latter case the group of exponent two is abelian identity shows that two distinct nonidentity elements a,b generate {e,a,b,ab}≅C2​×C2​.
For a group of order six, either an element generates it or some element a has order of a group element three: otherwise all nonidentity elements would be involutions, producing a four-element subgroup in contradiction with Lagrange's theorem. Pairing each element with its inverse element gives an involution b outside ⟨a⟩. The subgroup ⟨a⟩ has index of a subgroup two and is a normal subgroup, so bab−1=a or a−1. The commuting case makes ab have order of a group element six, whereas the second case gives the multiplication rules of S3​ on the six distinct elements ai,aib, 0≤i<3.
All these groups embed in S4​ except C5​ and C6​. The former is excluded by Lagrange's theorem; the latter is excluded because the disjoint cycle decomposition of a permutation of four letters cannot have least common multiple of cycle lengths equal to six.

Group of order six

Words: 159
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
Every group of order six is isomorphic to the cyclic group C6​ or the symmetric group on three points S3​. Lagrange's theorem restricts element orders to 1,2,3,6. If there is an element of order six, it generates the group. If every nonidentity element had order two, the group of exponent two is abelian result would produce a subgroup {e,a,b,ab} of order four, contradicting Lagrange's theorem. Thus the noncyclic case has an element x of order three.
There cannot be two distinct subgroups of order three: their intersection would be trivial and their nine pairwise products would be distinct elements of a six-element group. Hence exactly two elements have order three, and the other three nonidentity elements have order two. The subgroup ⟨x⟩ has index two and is normal. Choose an involution h outside it. Conjugation sends x to x or x−1. The first case would make xh have order six, so hxh−1=x−1. The generators therefore obey x3=h2=e, hxh−1=x−1, the relations realized by (123) and (12) in S3​.

Fitting subgroup (F(G))

Words: 196 Articles: 4
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
The largest nilpotent normal subgroup of a finite group G. If Op​(G) denotes its p-core, distinct p-cores commute, and F(G)=∏p​Op​(G). Every normal nilpotent group has Sylow subgroups which are characteristic subgroups, so it is contained in this product.

Fitting subgroup is self-centralizing in soluble groups

Words: 45
Fitting subgroup OurBigBook.com
In a finite soluble group, CG​(F(G))≤F(G). Put C=CG​(F) and D=C∩F=Z(F). If C>D, choose an elementary abelian minimal normal subgroup of G/D inside C/D, and let K be its preimage. Then K′≤D≤Z(K), so K is a nilpotent normal subgroup, contradicting K≤F.

Fitting subgroup centralizes the socle

Words: 59
Fitting subgroup OurBigBook.com
For a finite group, F(G) centralizes its group socle. A nonabelian minimal normal subgroup meets F(G) trivially: otherwise it is nilpotent, and its nontrivial characteristic center makes it abelian. Their group commutators therefore vanish. An abelian minimal normal subgroup M is an elementary abelian p-group; M≤Op​(G) and M∩Z(Op​(G))=1 by the fixed-point counting of a finite p-group on M. Minimal normality makes M≤Z(Op​(G)), and other p-cores commute with M.

Nilpotent normal subgroup

Words: 30
Fitting subgroup OurBigBook.com
A normal subgroup which is a nilpotent group. In a finite group its unique Sylow subgroups are characteristic subgroups and hence normal in the ambient group. Products of nilpotent normal subgroups are nilpotent groups: their normal Sylow subgroups of different prime characteristics commute.

p-core (Op​(G))

Words: 33
Fitting subgroup OurBigBook.com
The largest normal p-subgroup of a finite group. Products of normal p-subgroups are again normal p-subgroups, since ∣AB∣=∣A∣∣B∣/∣A∩B∣. Thus the subgroup generated by all such subgroups is itself a p-subgroup. It is a characteristic subgroup.

Classification of groups of order ten (C10​, D10​)

Words: 75
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
A group of order ten is either a cyclic group or the dihedral group of the pentagon. Lagrange's theorem and the fact that a group of exponent two has power-of-two order force an element of order five or ten. In the latter case the group is cyclic. In the former case its order-five cyclic subgroup is normal by index two; an outside involution acts on it either trivially or by inversion. The trivial action gives C5​×C2​≅C10​, and inversion gives D10​.

Almost simple group (T≤G≤Aut(T))

Words: 29
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
A group between a nonabelian simple group and its automorphism group. Finite two-transitive groups are either of this type or affine two-transitive groups, a structural theorem rather than an order-divisibility test.

Heisenberg group over a prime field (UT3​(Fp​))

Words: 180 Articles: 1
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
Upper-unitriangular three-by-three matrices over the prime finite field form the finite analogue of the real Heisenberg group. In coordinates their multiplication is (a,b,c)(a′,b′,c′)=(a+a′,b+b′,c+c′+ab′). The order is p3, and (a,b,c)k=(ka,kb,kc+(2k​)ab). For odd p, every nonidentity element has order p, but the group is nonabelian. For p=2 the exponent statement changes, so odd characteristic is essential for the nonisomorphic Gassmann equivalent regular subgroups construction.

Abelian plane subgroup of a finite Heisenberg group

Words: 121
Heisenberg group over a prime field OurBigBook.com
Use the coordinate convention
A(a,b,c)=​100​a10​bc1​​,a,b,c∈Fp​.
(1)
In this convention the Heisenberg group over a prime field has the product
A(a,b,c)A(a′,b′,c′)=A(a+a′,b+b′+ac′,c+c′).
(2)
The subset H={A(t,b,t):t,b∈Fp​} is an Abelian subgroup of order p2: the middle coordinate in a product is b+b′+tt′, which is symmetric in the factors. Also A(t,b,t)−1=A(−t,t2−b,−t) lies in H. The map A(a,b,c)↦a−c is a surjective group homomorphism to the additive group of Fp​, with kernel of a group homomorphism H. Hence H is a normal subgroup of subgroup index p, and its left cosets are exactly the level sets of a−c.
For odd p, an explicit group isomorphism from H to the additive group Fp2​ is
A(t,b,t)⟼(t,b−t2/2).
(3)
The term tt′ in matrix multiplication cancels the cross term in (t+t′)2/2. Thus H is an elementary abelian group, isomorphic to Cp​×Cp​.

Tetrahedral symmetry (T≅A4​,Td​≅S4​)

Words: 476 Articles: 4
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
A regular tetrahedron has a proper rotational symmetry group T of order 12, isomorphic to the alternating group A4​ acting on its four vertices. Its full spatial symmetry group Td​ has order 24 and is isomorphic to the symmetric group S4​; the additional operations reverse orientation. Three-fold vertex/face-axis rotations and half-turns about opposite-edge midpoints generate the proper group. The distinction matters when a field symmetry uses only proper rotations, but a scalar density also admits reflections.

Rotational symmetry group of a tetrahedron (T≅A4​)

Words: 25
Tetrahedral symmetry OurBigBook.com
The orientation-preserving symmetries of a regular tetrahedron form the alternating group on its four vertices. There are twelve elements: the identity, eight rotational symmetries of order three, and three half-turns.

Small subgroups of tetrahedral symmetry (25 subgroups with ∣H∣≤6)

Words: 211
Tetrahedral symmetry OurBigBook.com
The full symmetry group of a regular tetrahedron is the symmetric group S4​ acting on its vertices. Its subgroups with at most six elements have eight types up to conjugation, with the following representative subgroups and counts:
abstract groupC1​C2​C2​C3​C4​C2​×C2​C2​×C2​S3​​representative{e}⟨(12)⟩⟨(12)(34)⟩⟨(123)⟩⟨(1234)⟩{e,(12)(34),(13)(24),(14)(23)}⟨(12),(34)⟩{σ:σ(4)=4}​count16343134​​
(4)
A transposition is a reflection through the plane containing the two fixed vertices and the midpoint of the exchanged edge. A double transposition is a half-turn about the axis joining the midpoints of the two exchanged edges. A three-cycle is a one-third-turn about a vertex-to-opposite-face axis. A four-cycle is a quarter-turn composed with a reflection perpendicular to the opposite-edge midpoint axis; it is an improper orthogonal transformation.
The unique Klein four-group containing only double transpositions consists of the three opposite-edge half-turns and the identity element. The other three Klein four-groups consist of two perpendicular mirror reflections, their half-turn product, and the identity element. Each S3​ is a stabilizer subgroup of a vertex, including the three rotations and three mirror reflections preserving that vertex.
For completeness, a Klein four-group containing (12) must contain the commuting involution (34) or (12)(34), yielding the displayed subgroup; one containing no transpositions must contain all three double transpositions. An S3​ subgroup has a unique cyclic subgroup of cardinality three, whose unique fixed vertex must therefore be preserved by the entire S3​. These observations and the disjoint cycle decomposition exhaust the types allowed by groups of order at most six. The counts sum to 25.

Tetrahedral quotient onto the cyclic group of order three (A4​/V4​≅C3​)

Words: 83
Tetrahedral symmetry OurBigBook.com
The identity and three half-turns form a normal Klein four-group V4​ inside the proper rotational tetrahedral symmetry group A4​. Conjugation preserves double-transposition cycle type, establishing normality. The quotient group has order three and is therefore cyclic. If r is any 3-cycle, every element is uniquely rjk with j∈{0,1,2} and k∈V4​. The formula rjk↦e2πij/3 defines a surjective group homomorphism with kernel V4​. Normality allows the factors from V4​ to be moved past powers of r, making exponents add modulo three and proving the homomorphism property directly.

Tetrahedral rotation conjugacy classes (1,3,4,4)

Words: 84
Tetrahedral symmetry OurBigBook.com
The proper rotational tetrahedral symmetry group is A4​, acting by even permutations of the vertices. Its conjugacy classes consist of the identity, the three half-turns about opposite-edge midpoint axes, four rotations through +2π/3 about outward-pointing vertex axes, and their four inverses. A 3-cycle has a three-element centralizer, so its class has size 12/3=4. Conjugating it to its inverse would require an odd permutation on its three moved vertices, so the two orientations form different classes in A4​ even though they lie in one class in S4​.

Group of order eight (∣G∣=8)

Words: 87
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
Up to group isomorphism, the groups of order eight are C8​, C4​×C2​, C23​, D8​ and Q8​, with D8​ here denoting the eight-element dihedral group. An element of order eight gives the first case. If every nonidentity element has order two the group is an elementary abelian group. Otherwise, after excluding elements of order eight, a cyclic subgroup of order four has index two; an element outside it either commutes with its generator or inverts it. In the latter case its square is either the identity or the central involution, giving the dihedral group or quaternion group.

Feit–Thompson theorem

Words: 33
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
Every finite group of odd order is a solvable group. In particular, a nonabelian simple group has even order and therefore has an involution by Cauchy's theorem for finite groups. This is a deep theorem, not an elementary consequence of the Sylow theorems.

Finite group theory OurBigBook.com

Maximal subgroups of A5 (A4​, C5​⋊C2​, S3​)

Words: 71
Alternating group OurBigBook.com
Every maximal proper subgroup normalizes one of its minimal normal subgroups. As A5​ has no proper nonabelian simple subgroup, that subgroup is elementary abelian. Its possible types are C2​,C22​,C3​,C5​. Their normalizers have orders 4,12,6,10 respectively. The order-four normalizer lies in an order-twelve point stabilizer; the other three types are maximal and each forms a single conjugacy class. There are five, six and ten maximal subgroups of orders twelve, ten and six, respectively.

Automorphisms of alternating groups from triple supports (Aut(An​)≅Sn​(n≥5, n=6))

Words: 117
Alternating group OurBigBook.com
Except in degree six, the 3-cycles are characterized among order-three elements by the largest centralizer. Their cyclic subgroups correspond to three-element supports. Two different such subgroups commute exactly for disjoint supports; with one common point their generator products have order five, and with two common points those products have order two or three. Thus an automorphism induces an automorphism of J(n,3). The maximal cliques of a Johnson graph reconstruct a permutation of the points. After undoing that permutation, an automorphism fixes every cyclic 3-subgroup. Product orders force its choices of generator inversion to be consistent on the connected graph, and inversion of every 3-cycle would reverse a noncommuting product. Hence it fixes all 3-cycles, which generate An​.

Connected triple supports generate an alternating group

Words: 55
Alternating group OurBigBook.com
A connected finite hypergraph of three-element supports, with a three-cycle on each support, generates the full alternating group. To merge a new triple meeting an old alternating support in two letters, conjugate over unordered pairs of old letters. For one-letter overlap compare (abc) and (a′bc): their quotient is (aba′), reducing to two two-letter-overlap steps.

Conjugacy classes of the alternating group on six letters (∣A6​∣=360)

Words: 67
Alternating group OurBigBook.com
The alternating conjugacy class splitting criterion gives seven conjugacy classes in A6​. Their cycle types and sizes are 16:1, 2212:45, 313:40, 32:40, 42:90, and two 51 classes of size 72. Representatives of the split classes are a 5-cycle and its square. Their sizes sum to 360. A normal subgroup must be a union of these classes containing the identity, so these explicit sizes can prove simplicity using Lagrange's theorem.

Symmetric group on three points (S3​)

Words: 47
Symmetric group OurBigBook.com
The permutation group of a three-element set has six elements: the identity, three transpositions, and two three-cycles. A three-cycle and any transposition generate it, with relations x3=h2=e, hxh−1=x−1. Its alternating group is the normal cyclic subgroup of order three. It is the unique nonabelian isomorphism type of a group of order six.

Normal subgroups and quotients of the symmetric group on three letters

Words: 102
Symmetric group OurBigBook.com
The conjugacy classes of the symmetric group on three letters have sizes 1,3,2: the identity, the three transpositions and the two 3-cycles. A normal subgroup is a union of whole conjugacy classes and contains the identity. Its candidate orders are therefore 1,4,3,6. Lagrange's theorem excludes four, leaving precisely {e}, A3​ and S3​. The order-three subgroup is the cyclic group of the two 3-cycles and the identity; it is also the kernel of a group homomorphism of the sign map.
The first isomorphism theorem gives the corresponding quotients S3​, C2​ and the trivial group. Thus these are exactly the possible images of surjective group homomorphisms from S3​. Each occurs, by the identity map, the sign map and the constant identity map, respectively.

Automorphisms of the symmetric group

Words: 156 Articles: 1
Symmetric group OurBigBook.com
An automorphism preserving the transposition class is inner: commuting relations recover the vertex stars of the complete graph, with a small-case adjustment in degrees three and four. An involution class has the same size as the transposition class only in degree six, when triple transpositions also have size fifteen. Hence outer automorphism groups of symmetric groups are trivial outside degree six and have size at most two in degree six.

Symmetric-group involution class-size collision (n!/[2kk!(n−2k)!]=(2n​)⟺k=1 or (n,k)=(6,3))

Words: 86
Automorphisms of the symmetric group OurBigBook.com
A permutation of order two is a product of k disjoint transpositions. Its conjugacy class has the displayed size. For k≥2, equality with the transposition class requires (n−2)!/(n−2k)!=2k−1k!. The left side grows strictly with n. At n=2k, its ratio to the right side is one only for k=3; at k=2 it jumps from below to above one between n=4 and n=5, and for k≥4 it is already greater than one. Thus degree six is the only possible exceptional degree for an group automorphism not preserving transpositions.

Permutation group

Words: 127 Articles: 2
Symmetric group OurBigBook.com
A subgroup of the symmetric group of a set, acting faithfully by permutations. A finite permutation group specified by generators can be enumerated by repeatedly multiplying the elements already found by those generators until no new element appears. Its orbits and conjugacy classes can then be computed directly.

Substitution theory

Words: 23
Permutation group OurBigBook.com
The historical study of permutations of letters or quantities and their compositions, closely connected with the development of group theory and the theory of polynomial equations.

Oligomorphic permutation group

Words: 58
Permutation group OurBigBook.com
A permutation group on a set is oligomorphic when its diagonal action on ordered n-tuples has finitely many orbits for every positive integer n. For a countable model of a complete theory, an oligomorphic automorphism group makes every finite-arity type space finite: realized types are dense, and only finitely many are possible because types are constant on orbits.

For n≥2 and 1≤k<n, an n-cycle c=(12…n) and t=(11+k) generate Sn​ exactly when gcd(n,k)=1. Their conjugate transpositions connect labels differing by k modulo n. This graph is connected exactly at coprime separation, so transpositions on a connected graph generate the symmetric group. Otherwise residue classes modulo gcd(n,k) form a nontrivial block system preserved by both generators.

Prime-power characterization by full permutation cycles (∀σ∈Sn​: ord(σ)=n⟹σ is an n-cycle⟺n=pr)

Words: 91
Permutation cycle OurBigBook.com
For n>1, every permutation of order of a permutation n in Sn​ is one full cycle if and only if n is a prime power. If n=pr, all lengths in its disjoint cycle decomposition divide pr, and their least common multiple is their maximum. One cycle therefore has length n and uses every symbol. If n has more than one prime divisor, write n=ab with a,b>1 coprime by separating one full prime-power factor from the others. Since a+b≤ab=n, disjoint cycles of lengths a and b fit inside Sn​. Their product has order of a permutation lcm(a,b)=n, but is not a full cycle.

Disjoint cycle decomposition (σ=γ1​⋯γr​)

Words: 79
Permutation cycle OurBigBook.com
A disjoint cycle decomposition writes a permutation as a product of disjoint permutation cycles. Repeatedly apply the permutation to a point until it returns to that point; these successive points form one cycle. Repeat on points not yet used. Finiteness and injectivity ensure that each process returns to its starting point. This partitions the underlying finite set into cycles. The decomposition is unique up to reordering the cycles, cyclically rotating the entries within each cycle, and optionally omitting fixed-point one-cycles. Include the one-cycles when specifying cycle type.

Words: 62
Cycle type OurBigBook.com
Squaring an odd-length permutation cycle retains its length, whereas an even-length cycle splits into two cycles of half its length. Thus if any even cycle is present, the number of cycles strictly increases, so the cycle type changes. Since conjugate permutations in a symmetric group have the same cycle type, a permutation is conjugate to its square precisely when all its cycle lengths are odd, equivalently when its order of a group element is odd.

Left multiplication of a permutation by a transposition (a b) swaps the two target labels a,b. If they occur in different cycles, (a x1​…xp​)(b y1​…yq​) becomes the single cycle (a x1​…xp​ b y1​…yq​). If they occur in the same cycle, that formula reverses and splits the cycle in two. All other cycles are unchanged, so the total number of cycles, including fixed points, decreases or increases by exactly one. Empty intermediate lists yield one-cycles and require no exceptional case.

Quaternion group modulo its centre (Q8​/Z(Q8​)≅C2​×C2​)

Words: 94
Quaternion group OurBigBook.com
In the quaternion group, −1=i2=j2=k2 commutes with each generator because any element commutes with its powers. Hence N={1,−1} is central and is a normal subgroup. The reverse products satisfy ji=−k, kj=−i, ik=−j, so none of ±i,±j,±k is central. Therefore Z(Q8​)=N.
The four cosets are N,iN,jN,kN. Each nonidentity coset squares to N, and (iN)(jN)=kN. Thus the quotient group is the Klein four-group. Explicitly, mapping ±1 to its identity and mapping ±i,±j,±k to its three different nonidentity elements is a surjective group homomorphism with group kernel N. The first isomorphism theorem gives the title result.

Character table of the quaternion group

Words: 96
Quaternion group OurBigBook.com
The quaternion group has conjugacy classes {1}, {−1}, {±i}, {±j}, {±k}, with sizes 1,1,2,2,2. Over the complex numbers, the number of classes and the sum of squares of irreducible representation dimensions force four one-dimensional representations and one two-dimensional representation. For ϵ,η∈{±1}, the linear character rows on these classes are (1,1,ϵ,η,ϵη). Orthogonality then gives the remaining row (2,−2,0,0,0). A representation with character (4,−4,0,0,0) contains two copies of the two-dimensional irrep and none of the linear irreps, by the character inner product. The choice of scalar field matters: the corresponding quaternionic four-dimensional real representation is irreducible over the reals.

This rules out a faithful group action, even with several group orbits. The regular action on eight points is faithful by Cayley theorem.

Finite p-groups are nilpotent

Words: 79
Finite p-group OurBigBook.com
Induct on the order of the finite p-group. Its center of a group is nontrivial unless the group itself is trivial. Quotient by the center to obtain a smaller finite p-group and lift a central series supplied by induction. Prepending the center gives a central series for the original group: the first term is central, and the remaining commutator-containment conditions are exactly the lifted quotient conditions. Hence every finite p-group is a nilpotent group. Since central factors are Abelian, every nilpotent group is also a soluble group.

Words: 81
Simple group OurBigBook.com
For a finite simple group with a subgroup of index n≥3, the coset action is nontrivial and its kernel is a normal subgroup, hence trivial. Its sign homomorphism must also be trivial: otherwise simplicity would give an isomorphism to C2​, which cannot act transitively on at least three points. Thus the image lies in the alternating group. In particular Lagrange's theorem gives ∣G∣∣n!/2. This can exclude simplicity with very little counting: a group of order 112 has a subgroup of index seven by Sylow theorems, but 112 does not divide 7!/2.

Soluble simple group has prime order

Simple group OurBigBook.com
For a nontrivial simple soluble group, the commutator subgroup is either the identity or the whole group. It cannot be the whole group because the derived series would never terminate. The group is therefore Abelian. Every nonidentity element then generates a normal cyclic subgroup, which must be the whole group. An infinite cyclic group has proper nontrivial subgroups; a finite cyclic group is simple exactly when its order is prime. Thus the soluble simple groups are precisely the cyclic groups of prime order.

Simple group OurBigBook.com
For a finite simple group of this order, e=0 gives a normal Sylow 5-subgroup, and e=1 gives a nontrivial sign homomorphism from the regular action, because an involution swaps fifteen pairs. Thus e≥2. The Sylow 2-count divides 15; it cannot be one or three. If it is five, a Sylow subgroup's normalizer has index five. If it is fifteen, the strengthened Sylow congruence from intersections produces two Sylow subgroups meeting in index two. Their common subgroup is normal in both, so its normalizer contains both and has index three or five. Simplicity excludes index three. The resulting faithful degree-five action embeds G in A5​ and forces order 60, proving the conclusion.

Let Dn​ act on Euclidean space by rotations through 2π/n about a vertical axis and half-turns about n equally spaced horizontal axes. A round solid torus about the vertical axis, drilled through radially along the 2n places where the horizontal axes cross its tube, has a smooth boundary of genus 2n+1 after equivariant rounding of its rims. All nonidentity rotation axes lie in the complement of this boundary, so the induced group action is a free action of a group. Each bore replaces two closed discs by an annulus, lowering Euler characteristic by two and increasing genus by one. The boundary orientation is preserved; its induced Riemann surface has an unramified quotient space of genus two by the Riemann-Hurwitz formula.

Sylow theorems OurBigBook.com
Let p<q be distinct prime numbers. Every group of group order p2q2 is Abelian if and only if p does not divide q2−1.
For sufficiency, the Sylow theorems make the number of Sylow p-subgroups one of 1,q,q2, congruent to one modulo p. The divisibility hypothesis excludes both nontrivial choices, so that subgroup is normal. The number of Sylow subgroups for q is one of 1,p,p2, congruent to one modulo q. The choice p is impossible because p<q. If q divided p2−1=(p−1)(p+1), primality and q>p would force q=p+1, hence (p,q)=(2,3); this pair violates the hypothesis. Thus the other Sylow subgroup is normal too. Their intersection is trivial, and their group commutators lie in that intersection, so the group is their direct product of groups. A group of prime-square order is abelian: its nontrivial center of a group is either the whole group or has cyclic quotient, and a cyclic central quotient also forces commutativity. Both factors are therefore abelian.
For necessity, suppose p∣q2−1. The multiplicative group of a finite field is cyclic, so Fq2×​ contains α of order p. Let the cyclic group Cp2​ act on the additive group of Fq2​ by mapping its generator to multiplication by α. This is a well-defined nontrivial group action, since αp2=1. The resulting semidirect product has order p2q2 and is nonabelian, because the generator does not commute with a nonzero field element. Thus a nonabelian group of this order exists exactly when p∣q2−1.

Sylow theorems OurBigBook.com
The Sylow 2-subgroups of S3​ are its three transposition subgroups, while its unique Sylow 3-subgroup is A3​. The three Sylow 2-subgroups of S4​ are dihedral groups of order eight and are the normalizers of the three cyclic subgroups generated by inverse pairs of 4-cycles. The five Sylow 2-subgroups of A5​ are Klein four-groups, one fixing each letter.

Sylow containment from a coset fixed point

Words: 42
Sylow theorems OurBigBook.com
If P is a Sylow p-subgroup of G and Q is any p-subgroup, let Q act on G/P. Since p does not divide ∣G/P∣, some coset gP is fixed. Hence g−1Qg≤P, or equivalently Q≤gPg−1.

Sylow counts in a faithful degree-seven action with S4 point stabilizers

Words: 75
Sylow theorems OurBigBook.com
Suppose a group acts faithfully and transitively on seven points, every point stabilizer is S4​, and every two-point stabilizer is a Klein four-group. Then the group has order 168 and
n2​=21,n3​=28,n7​=8.
(14)
Count pairs consisting of a point and a Sylow subgroup fixing it for p=2,3; the two-point stabilizer ensures uniqueness. For p=7, a normal Sylow subgroup would force the group into its order-42 normalizer in S7​.

Even-involution coset fixed-point lemma

Words: 67
Sylow theorems OurBigBook.com
Suppose a finite group G has no index-two subgroup, P is a Sylow 2-subgroup, H has index two in P, and x∈G has order two. The sign of the action on G/H defines a homomorphism G→{±1} and is therefore trivial. Since [G:H]≡2(mod4), a fixed-point-free involution would be an odd number of transpositions. Thus x fixes a coset gH, equivalently g−1xg∈H.

Cauchy theorem for groups

Words: 144 Articles: 1
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
If a prime divides the order of a finite group, the group contains an element of that prime order.
One proof lets a cyclic group of order p rotate the tuples
(x1​,…,xp​)withx1​⋯xp​=1.
(15)
The tuple set has size ∣G∣p−1, and its fixed tuples are precisely (x,…,x) with xp=1. Counting nonfixed orbits modulo p forces a nonidentity fixed tuple.

Cyclic-tuple proof of Cauchy theorem (#{g:gp=1}≡∣G∣p−1(modp))

Words: 83
Cauchy theorem for groups OurBigBook.com
For a prime divisor p of the order of a finite group, rotate the tuples (g1​,…,gp​) whose product is the identity. Rotation preserves that constraint even for a nonabelian group, by conjugating the product. Every nonfixed orbit has p elements, while the fixed tuples correspond to gp=1. There are ∣G∣p−1 tuples, so the number of fixed tuples is divisible by p. Since the identity is one, another solution exists and has order exactly p. This supplies an elementary proof of Cauchy theorem for groups.

Power-map criterion for a finite group

Words: 50
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
For a finite group G, the map x↦xm is bijective exactly when m is coprime to ∣G∣. If the two numbers are coprime, an inverse exponent modulo ∣G∣ gives an inverse map. If a prime p divides both, the Cauchy theorem for groups supplies a nonidentity element sent to the identity.

Composition series

Words: 302 Articles: 5
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
A composition series is a finite subnormal chain whose successive quotients are simple.

Exactly two composition series for a simple group times a prime cyclic group (G=S×Cp​,S nonabelian simple)

Words: 97
Composition series OurBigBook.com
The only nontrivial proper normal subgroups of this direct product of groups are its two factors. Indeed a normal subgroup meeting S×1 nontrivially contains it by the simple group property. Otherwise each of its commutators with S×1 lies in that trivial intersection. Its first coordinates therefore lie in Z(S)=1, so it is contained in 1×Cp​. Both factors are simple and each quotient by one factor is isomorphic to the other. Hence precisely two composition series occur, one through each factor. This is compatible with the Jordan–Hölder theorem, since the two series have the same simple factors in opposite orders. For S=A5​,p=2, the group has order 120.

Composition chains in products with S5 (ℓ(C2​×S5​)=3,ℓ(S5​×S5​)=4)

Words: 115
Composition series OurBigBook.com
The sign quotient of S5​ controls its cyclic composition factors, while its unique nontrivial proper normal subgroup A5​ supplies the nonabelian factor. There are four composition chains in C2​×S5​: the three maximal normal subgroups are the kernels of the nonzero maps to C2​, and only C2​×A5​ has two choices for its next term. In S5​×S5​ there are eight chains: six pass through A5​×A5​ and one of its two simple direct factors; two instead pass through a single S5​ direct factor. The equal-sign subgroup gives two of the six chains. It has no quotient A5​, since its odd diagonal element acts by an outer automorphism on either alternating factor.

Composition length (ℓ(M))

Words: 27
Composition series OurBigBook.com
The composition length of a finite-length module or group is the number of simple factors in a composition series. The Jordan–Hölder theorem makes this independent of the chosen composition series.

Jordan–Hölder factor

Words: 50 Articles: 1
Composition series OurBigBook.com
A Jordan–Hölder factor is a simple quotient in a composition series. The Jordan–Hölder theorem says that the multiset of such factors is independent of the chosen composition series.

Jordan–Hölder theorem

Words: 25
Jordan–Hölder factor OurBigBook.com
Any two composition series of a finite group or finite-length module have the same length and the same simple factors up to permutation and isomorphism.

Klein four-group

Words: 264 Articles: 3
Finite group theory OurBigBook.com
The Klein four-group is the abelian group with three nonidentity elements, all of order two.

Character table of the Klein four-group (χpq​(aubv)=(−1)pu+qv)

Words: 86
Klein four-group OurBigBook.com
Write the Klein four-group as {1,a,b,ab}. Its four one-dimensional irreducible representations independently assign signs to a,b, so the displayed characters have p,q∈{0,1}. The character table is
χ00​χ01​χ10​χ11​​11111​a11−1−1​b1−11−1​ab1−1−11​​.
(16)
Every conjugacy class is a singleton because the group is abelian. The four rows exhaust the complex irreducibles by the equality between their number and the number of classes. If H is this table, HHT=4I proves character orthogonality. The diagonal three-dimensional representation by half-turns about the coordinate axes is the direct sum of the three nontrivial characters, with total character (3,−1,−1,−1).

Group generated by sign reversal and reciprocation (a(x)=−x,b(x)=1/x,a2=b2=e,ab=ba)

Words: 67
Klein four-group OurBigBook.com
On the nonzero real numbers, sign reversal a and reciprocation b are commuting involutions. Their function composition generates exactly e(x)=x, a(x)=−x, b(x)=1/x and ab(x)=−1/x. The relations a2=b2=e and ab=ba identify the group with C2​×C2​, the Klein four-group. Its subgroups are the trivial group, its three order-two cyclic subgroups and itself. Excluding zero from the domain is necessary for all four transformations to be defined and invertible.

Equivalent sheared representations of the Klein four-group

Words: 96
Klein four-group OurBigBook.com
Let the Klein four-group have generators X,Y and Z=XY, with X2=Y2=I and XY=YX. For every real p, the matrices
D(X)=−I2​,D(Y)=(−10​−p1​),D(Z)=−D(Y)
(17)
define a group representation. Indeed, D(Y)2=I2​, and D(X) commutes with every matrix, so the group relations hold.
Set S=(10​−p/21​). A direct change of basis gives
S−1D(Y)S=diag(−1,1),S−1D(Z)S=diag(1,−1).
(18)
Consequently all these representations are isomorphic representations, with character values (2,−2,0,0) on (I,X,Y,Z). Each is a direct sum of the two one-dimensional representations whose values on X are −1 and whose values on Y are +1 and −1. A group representation need not be orthogonal; nonzero p changes the basis rather than the represented group.
